For it was not fitting that, when he was being betrayed, he should be seized from that place where he had eaten the Passover with the disciples. But it was fitting also that, before he was betrayed, he should pray and, for praying, should choose a clean place for the prayer; for he knew that, just as air differs from purer air, so does the earth of a holy place differ from that of a holier…
For it was not fitting that He should be seized in the place where He had sate and eaten the Passover with His disciples. Also He must first pray, and choose a place pure for prayer.
He who had received five talents comes first with boldness before his Lord.

For the Saints who have wrought right works, shall receive in recompense of their right works the King's right hand, at which is rest and glory; but the wicked for their evil and sinister deeds have fallen to the left hand, that is, into the misery of torments. Then shall the King say to those who are on his right hand, Come, that in whatsoever they are behind they may make it up when they are more perfectly united to Christ. He adds, ye blessed of my Father, to show how eminendy blessed they were, being of old blessed of the Lord, which made heaven and earth. (Ps. 115:15.)

Receive the kingdom which has been prepared for you from the foundation of the world. (What in the Latin reads from the foundation of the world, in the Greek reads thus: from the laying-down of the world; and he expounds according to the Greek expression what according to the Latin it was not fitting to expound.) But why the Scriptures frequently use the term "laying-down" in reference to the world — as here too, saying from the laying-down of the world — let him inquire who is able, knowing that not everything which has been created is called a "laying-down," nor is it written anywhere of "the laying-down" of the thrones or dominions or principalities. But if one gathers together the term "laying-down" from all its occurrences, in case perhaps it has been said in some other place, and compares those places with the things that are said about the laying-down of the world, ascending by…

But when all these shall have been fulfilled, then not the earth only but the heavens also shall pass away; that is, not only the men whose life is earthy, and who are therefore called the earth, but also they whose conversation is in heaven, and who are therefore called the heaven; these shall pass away to things to come, that they may come to better things. But the words spoken by the Saviour shall not pass away, because they effect and shall ever effect their purpose; but the perfect and they that admit no further improvement, passing through what they are, come to that which they are not; and this is that, My words shall not pass away. And perhaps the words of Moses and the Prophets have passed away, because all that they prophesied has been fulfilled; but the words of Christ are always complete, daily fulfilling and to be fulfilled in the saints. Or perhaps we ought not to say that…

Great things were done at the moment that Jesus cried with a great voice.

It is understood that there were two veils; one veiling the Holy of Holies, the other, the outer part of the tabernacle or temple. In the Passion then of our Lord and Saviour, it was the outer veil which was rent from the top to the bottom, that by the rending of the veil from the beginning to the end of the world, the mysteries might be published which had been hid with good reason until the Lord's coming. But when that which is perfect is come, (1 Cor. 13:10.) then the second veil also shall be taken away, that we may see the things that are hidden within, to wit, the true Ark of the Testament, and behold the Cherubim and the rest in their real nature.

These same mighty works are still done every day; the veil of the temple is rent for the Saints, in order to reveal the things that are contained within. The…

If somebody, in the whole body of the congregations of the church, is industrious and handy for practical action and he changes and his hand causes him to sin, the eye should say to this hand, "I have no need of you." And after it has said it, let him cut it off and throw it from him. All will still be well if his head is still blessed and his feet worthy of his blessed head, so that the head, doing its duty, may not be able to say to the feet, "I have no need of you." But if some foot is found which is a temptation to sin for the whole body, the head should say to this foot, "I have no need of you," and should cut it off and throw it away from him. It is far better for the rest of the body to go on into life lacking the foot or hand that offers temptation to sin than for the whole body to be exposed to temptation and to be sent into eternal fire with two whole feet or hands. Likewise…

That He says of John, Elias is already come, is not to be understood of the soul of Elias, that we fall not into the doctrine of metempsychosis, which is foreign to the truth of Church doctrine, but, as the Angel had foretold, he came in the spirit and power of Elias.

By this act Jesus showed himself to be "meek and lowly in heart," coming to those inferior to him, doing all that followed in order to humble himself and become obedient "unto death." It is not always the case that the one who baptizes is greater than the one who is baptized. Ananias was not greater than Paul. And while Philip baptized, Peter gave the Spirit through the laying on of hands.

Or, the sleep He now bids His disciples take is of a different sort from that which is related above to have befallen them. Then He found them sleeping, not taking repose, but because their eyes were heavy, but now they are not merely to sleep, but to take their rest, that this order may be rightly observed, namely, that we first watch with prayer that we enter not into temptation, and afterwards sleep and take our rest, when having found a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, (Ps. 132:3.) we may go up into our bed, and give sleep to our eyes. It may be also that the soul, unable to sustain a continual energy by reason of its union with the flesh, may blamelessly admit some relaxations, which may be the moral interpretation of slumbers, and then again after due time be quickened to new energy.

And then, coming, he said to his disciples: sleep now and rest; behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go; behold, he who will betray me has drawn near (26, 45. 46). Then — without doubt after the third prayer. But that sleep, which he now orders his disciples to sleep, is not the same as the one that is written above to have twice befallen the disciples. For there he "found them sleeping" but not also resting, and "again he found them sleeping" with their eyes weighed down; but now he commands them not simply to sleep, but with rest. For to sleep and rest according to the command of Christ differs greatly from a sleeping against the will of him who says: "remain here and keep watch with me" and who reproaches them on account of their sleep and says: "so, could you not watch one hour with me?" Therefore he did not…

Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of sinners. On account of this hour, I think, he also said to his mother: "My hour has not yet come". For here too he teaches that the approaching hour was bringing this about, that the Son of Man should be betrayed into the hands of sinners. Would that Jesus had then been betrayed into the hands of those sinners only! But as it is, I think that Jesus is always betrayed into the hands of sinners, whenever those who seem to believe in Jesus have Jesus in their hands while being sinners. But also, as often as a righteous man who has Jesus within himself is brought into the power of sinners who do to him what they can, Jesus is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

All who thus ask questions of any teacher to try him, and not to learn of him, we must regard as brethren of this Pharisee, according to what is said below, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of mine, ye have done it unto me. (Matt. 25:40.)

The bread that they had before they crossed the lake was no longer of any use to them when they reached the other side. They needed one kind of bread before they crossed and a different kind afterward. They forgot to take any loaves with them because they were careless about carrying bread. The disciples of Jesus had also crossed to another side. They had passed from the material to the spiritual, from the sensory to the intellectual. This is why Jesus said to them after the crossing, be careful and be on your guard.The Pharisees and Sadducees offered a different dough of teaching, a truly ancient yeast restricted to the bare letter and therefore not free from evil. Jesus does not want his disciples to eat of it any longer. Instead, he mixed a new spiritual dough when he himself offered to any who would abandon the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees and come to him, the living bread…

Peter had heard the word of Christ when He said, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell all that thou hast. Then he observed that the young man had departed sorrowful, and considered the difficulty of riches entering into the kingdom of heaven; and thereupon he put this question confidently as one who had achieved no easy matter. For though what he with his brother had left behind them were but little things, yet were they not esteemed as little with God, who considered that out of the fulness of their love they had so forsaken those least things, as they would have forsaken the greatest things if they had had them. So Peter, thinking rather of his will than of the intrinsic value of the sacrifice, asked Him confidently, Behold, we have left all.

It may be said, In all things which the Father revealed to Peter that the Son was, righteousness, sanctification, and the like, in all we have…

Or otherwise; And if one minister the divine word, knowing that it is Christ that makes it to be fruitful, such a one professes himself a minister and not a master; whence it follows, He that is greatest among you, let him be your servant. As Christ Himself, who was in truth our Master, professed Himself a minister, saying, I am in the midst of you as one that ministers. (Luke 22:27.) And well does He conclude this prohibition of all vain-glory with the words, And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Whenever you see of those who have received from Christ a dispensation of the oracles of God that some have more and some less; that some have not in comparison of the better sort half an understanding of things; that others have still less; you will perceive the difference of those who have all of them received from Christ oracles of God. They to whom five talents were given, and they to whom two, and they to whom one, have divers degrees of capacity, and one could not hold the measure of another; he who received but one having received no mean endowment, for one talent of such a master is a great thing. His proper servants are three, as there are three sorts of those that bear fruit. He that received five talents, is he that is able to raise all the meanings of the Scriptures to their more divine significations; he that has two is he that has been taught carnal doctrine, (for two…

But how should the people of Christ be hated by the nations who dwelt in the uttermost parts of the earth? But one may perhaps say, that in this place all is put hyperbolically for many. But this that He says, Then shall they deliver you, presents some difficulty; for before these things the Christians were delivered to tribulation. To this it may be answered, that at that time the Christians shall be more delivered to tribulation than ever. And persons in any misfortune love to examine into the origin of them, and to talk about them. Hence when the worship of the Gods shall be almost deserted by reason of the multitude of Christians, it will be said that that is the cause of the wars, and famines, and pestilences; and of the earthquakes also they will say that the Christians are the cause, whence the persecution of the Churches.

And that, Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's…
Peter followed Him afar off, He would neither keep close to Him, nor altogether leave Him, but followed afar off.

Now Peter was following him at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the chief priest, and having gone inside he was sitting with the servants to see the outcome of the matter.

Now while the master was being led away, Peter indeed was following, yet he could not follow him from close at hand, but from afar off, neither departing from him altogether nor walking along with him, nor beside him but following at a distance he came to the courtyard of the chief priest. And having gone inside, Peter was sitting within, neither ministering according to what those servants did nor doing the things which Jesus had taught, but he was awaiting the outcome of all these things, wishing to see it, since as yet he did not understand nor see the outcome of Christ's dispensations, toward what they were tending. Let him then be without blame who binds or looses another, that he may be found worthy to bind or loose in heaven. Moreover, to him who shall be able by his virtues to shut the gates of hell, are given in reward the keys of the kingdom of heaven. For every kind of virtue when any has begun to practise it, as it were opens itself before Him, the Lord, namely, opening it through His grace, so that the same virtue is found to be both the gate, and the key of the gate. But it may be that each virtue is itself the kingdom of heaven.

Or otherwise; With all thy heart, that is, in all recollection, act, thought; with all thy soul, to be ready, that is, to lay it down for God's religion; with all thy mind, bringing forth nothing but what is of God. And consider whether you cannot thus take the heart of the understanding, by which we contemplate things intellectual, and the mind of that by which we utter thoughts, walking as it were with the mind through each expression, and uttering it.

You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your mind, and with all your soul, and with all your strength. You shall love your neighbor as yourself — not the neighbor with all the heart, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and with all the mind. Again, he says: Love your enemies — and he did not add, "with all the heart." The divine word is not disordered, nor does it command impossible things, nor say, "Love your enemies as yourselves," but only, "Love your enemies"; it is enough for them that we love them and do not hold them in hatred. But the neighbor, as yourself. And God, with all the heart, and with all the soul, and with all the mind, and with all the strength.

Judas is interpreted CONFESSOR. Since, therefore, there are two disciples of Christ named by this name, inasmuch as Luke the evangelist counts among the twelve apostles that there were "Judas of James and Judas Iscariot," and since nothing with Christ is empty of a mystery, I judge that these two Judases were, in a mystery, figures of the Christians who confess the faith of Christ. Of these, one part indeed remains faithfully with Christ, whose mystery was Judas of James. But the other part, after it has believed and confessed the faith of Christ, on account of avarice forsakes Christ and, having become a…

If it be asked why Judas betrayed Jesus with a kiss, according to some it was because He desired to keep up the reverence due to his Master, and did not dare to make an open assault upon Him; according to others, it was out of fear that if he came as an avowed enemy, he might be the cause of His escape, which he believed Jesus had it in His power to effect. But I think that all betrayers of truth love to assume the guise of truth, and to use the sign of a kiss. Like Judas also, all heretics call Jesus Rabbi, and receive from Him mild answer.

Or, Pilate spoke this affirmatively, as he afterwards wrote in the inscription, The King of the Jews. By answering to the Chief Priest, Thou hast said, He indirectly reproved his doubts, but now He turns Pilate's speech into an affirmative, Jesus saith unto him, Thou sayest it.

But Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor questioned him, saying: Are you the king of the Jews? Jesus says to him: You say so. Truly Jesus "did not count it robbery that he was equal to God", and not once but frequently he humbled himself for the sake of men. And now therefore, having been "appointed judge of all creation" by the Father, the King of kings and Lord of lords, see to how great a degree he humbled himself, so that he consented to stand before the judge of the land of Judea at that time, and being summoned he was questioned with a question which Pilate perhaps in derision or in doubt asked, saying: Are you the king of the Jews? To which question he answered what he thought fitting, saying You say so. And when he was put on oath by the high priest, that he should say whether he himself is the Christ the Son of God, he answered: "You have said it", but when…
And observe, He says not vultures or crows, but eagles, showing the lordliness and royalty of all who have believed in the Lord's passion.

Or, when they allege secret and before unpublished Scriptures, in proof of their lie, they seem to say, Lo, the word of truth is in the desert. But when they produce canonical Scripture in which all Christians agree, they seem to say, Lo, the word of truth is in the chambers. Or wishing to point out such discourses as are altogether without Scripture, He said, If they shall say to you, Lo, he is in the secret chambers, believe it not. Truth is like the lightning that cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west. Or this may mean, that truth can be supported out of every passage of Scripture. The lightning of truth comes out of the east, that is, from the first beginnings of Christ, and shines throughout even to His passion, which is His setting; or from the very beginning of creation, to the last Scripture of the Apostles. I have previously quoted some of the words of Isaiah that precede the verse quoted in the Gospel and some of the words that follow the verse quoted in the Gospel. The word also promises to "close the eyes both of their prophets and their rulers" who claim to "see the hidden things."I suppose that these very things happened after the Savior had dwelt with these people. For "all the words," the words of the Scriptures in their entirety and also those of Isaiah, became to them "as the words of a sealed book." Now the word sealed was said as if the book was sealed with obscurity and not opened with clarity. The book is unclear to those who right from the start are "not able to…

Yet the words in which Peter and those in which Satan are rebuked, are not, as is commonly thought, the same; to Peter it is said, Get thee behind me, Satan; that is, follow me, thou that art contrary to my will; to the Devil it is said, Go thy way, Satan, understanding not 'behind me,' but 'into everlasting fire.' He said therefore to Peter, Get thee behind me, as to one who through ignorance was ceasing to walk after Christ. And He called him Satan, as one, who through ignorance had somewhat contrary to God. But he is blessed to whom Christ turns, even though He turn in order to rebuke him. But why said He to Peter, Thou art an offence unto me, (Ps. 119:165.) when in the Psalm it is said, Great peace have they that love thy law, and there is no offence to them? It must be answered, that not only is Jesus not offended, but neither is any man who is perfect in the love of God; and yet…

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful, but within are full of the bones of the dead and of every foulness. So you also outwardly indeed appear righteous to men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity (23, 27. 28).

For just as above "within they are full of plunder and intemperance," so likewise here also they are full of hypocrisy and iniquity, which are compared to the bones of the dead and to every uncleanness. For hypocrisy, since it is a certain pretense of good, has indeed nothing living from that good which it feigns, but has (so to speak) the bone of that virtue which it feigns. … the righteousness or chastity is dead. For if we hear wisely what the present discourse wishes to show, we understand that all feigned righteousness is dead righteousness, or rather is not even…

Then they crucified with him two robbers, one on the right and one on the left.

The Lord, crucified among robbers like the robbers themselves, fulfilled the prophecy that says of him: "and he was reckoned among the wicked". And it is possible to see his disciples, giving testimony to the worship of God which was introduced through him, being reckoned "among the wicked" and being crucified with them, or enduring the remaining sufferings, just as those men did. For the world and the spirit that is in it always persecutes the highest men and punishes indeed the highest in wickedness for the benefit of the many, but the highest in virtue, because this world is not worthy of those who consider not "the things that are seen", but "the things that are not seen", and who despise it, just as also of old the saints walked "in sheepskins and in goatskins, destitute, afflicted, wandering in…
The thief who was saved may be a sign of those who after many sins have believed on Christ.

This seems to be so like a warning He had given above, that a man might easily say that the Lord now repeated what He had said before; yet is it not so; He had not before said that He must be betrayed, but we hear now not only that He must be betrayed, but that He must be betrayed into the hands of men. The Son of Man indeed was delivered up by God the Father according to the Apostle (Rom. 8:32.), but different powers gave him up into the hands of men.

As for these matters let us inquire by what person or persons He will be delivered up into the hands of men; for there we are taught of whom He will suffer, and in what place He will suffer; but here, in addition, we learn that while His suffering many things takes place at the hands of the aforesaid, they are not the prime causes of His suffering many things, but the one or ones who delivered Him up into the hands of men. For some one will say that the Apostle, interpreting this, says with reference to God, "He that spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all; " but the Son also gave Himself to death for us, so that He was delivered up, not only by the Father but also by Himself. But another will say not merely that, but also collecting the passages together, will say that the Son is first delivered up by God,-then about to be tempted, then to be in conflict, then to suffer…

quotes.quote: Or because in six days this whole visible world was made; so he who is above all the things of this world, may ascend into the high mountain, and there see the glory of the Word of God.

Now at the feast day the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whomever they wished.

Do not be surprised if, the Roman rule still being in its beginnings among them, and the Jews newly taking up the yoke of the Romans, since it had been granted to the Jews that at the paschal solemnity they might ask for one whom they wished,

even though he seemed liable for a thousand murders. For thus the nations render certain favors to those whom they subject to themselves, until their yoke is confirmed over them. Yet this custom of releasing a prisoner existed at one time also among the Jews. For when Saul had decreed that no one should take food, but Jonathan had tasted a honeycomb against the king's decree, he found Jonathan liable; and although he was his appointed son, yet on account of some oath of his he had decreed to put him to death. But he did not kill him,…

Thus do the Gentiles show favours to those whom they subject to themselves, until their yoke is riveted. Yet did this practice obtain also among the Jews, Saul did not put Jonathan to death, because all the people sought his life. (1 Sam. 14.)

The Lord did not allow that He was a hard man as the servant supposed, but He assented to all his other words. But He is indeed hard to those who abuse the mercy of God to suffer themselves to become remiss, and use it not to be converted.

When the Savior says, "O faithless and perverse generation," he shows that wickedness has entered us through perversity, that it is contrary to nature and makes us perverse. And I think that he was irked at the whole human race on earth for its wickedness. So he said, "How long am I to bear with you?"

Or; Because the disciples could not heal him as being weak in faith, He said to them, O faithless generation, adding perverse, to show that their perverseness had introduced evil beyond their nature. But I suppose, that because of the perverseness of the whole human race, as it were oppressed with their evil nature, He said, How long shall I be with you?

Pilate says to them: What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ? They all say: Let him be crucified, and so on.

Wishing to strike into them shame at so great a wickedness, Pilate says to them: What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ, and not only this but also wishing to take the full measure of their impiety. But they, neither blushing at the fact that Pilate confessed Jesus to be Christ nor keeping any limit in their impiety, all said: Let him be crucified. And indeed, if they had asked that Barabbas be released, but had not on the contrary also demanded Christ for the cross — that is, if they had asked that Barabbas be acquitted, but had not asked that this man be crucified but had left him in Pilate's power, so that he might do with him what he willed — it would still have been of great impiety, that, leaving aside the just man, they had asked for a murderer.…

And having received the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own new tomb which he had hewn out in the rock, and rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb and departed (27, 59. 60). In wrapping it in a clean linen cloth and laying it in a new tomb, where no dead man had lain, he was preserving the body of Jesus for an exceptional resurrection. But I think rather that that linen cloth possessed greater cleanness from the fact that the body of Christ was wrapped in it than it had before; for the body of Jesus, even set in death, cleansed—as the body of Jesus—everything whatsoever it touched, and all the more made new that new tomb which had been hewn in the rock. And do not suppose that it was written by chance and said by mere happenstance, that he wrapped the body in a clean linen cloth and laid it in a new tomb, and that that tomb had been hewn in the…

This is no casual mention of the circumstances that the body was wrapped in clean linen, and laid in a new tomb, and a great stone rolled to the mouth, but that every thing touching the body of Jesus is clean, and new, and very great.

And sitting down they kept watch over him there. For "he was seen by Cephas, then by the eleven, then he appeared to more than five hundred brethren at once", "and last of all" by Paul. He spoke of "the shadow of death" and not simply "death." This is because of the inability of sin utterly to corrupt the soul. Such complete corruption happens to bodies in death. But sin brings forth the shadow of death. And the words "light is sprung up" signify that it did not spring up upon us who were looking for it, but it shone upon those who were unprepared for it.

But how can he who has been converted, and become as a little child, be yet liable to be scandalized? This may be thus explained. Every one who believes on the Son of God, and walks after evangelic acts, is converted and walks as a little child; but he who is not converted that he may become as a child, it is impossible that he should enter into the kingdom of heaven. But in every congregation of believers, there are some only newly converted that they may become as little children, but not yet made such; these are the little ones in Christ, and these are they that receive offence.

And His sisters, are they not all with us?" [Matthew 13:55-56] They thought, then, that He was the son of Joseph and Mary. quotes.quote: As the fig has its vital powers torpid within it through the season of winter, but when that is past its branches become tender by those very powers and put forth leaves; so the world and all those who are saved had before Christ's coming their vital energies dormant within them as in a season of winter. Christ's Spirit breathing upon them makes the branches of their hearts soft and tender, and that which was dormant within burgeons into leaf, and makes show of fruit. To such the summer and the coming of the glory of the Word of God is nigh at hand.

If the Lord had given no answer to the Pharisee who thus tempted Him, we should have judged that there was no commandment greater than the rest. But when the Lord adds, This is the first and great commandment, we learn how we ought to think of the commandments, that there is a great one, and that there are less down to the least. And the Lord says not only that it is a great, but that it is the first commandment, not in order of Scripture, but in supremacy of value. They only take upon them the greatness and supremacy of this precept, who not only love the Lord their God, but add these three conditions.

They that believe rightly, and live righteously, are likened to the five wise; they that profess the faith of Jesus, but prepare themselves not by good works to salvation, are likened to the five foolish.

And because the virtues are so linked together, that he who has one has all, so all the senses so follow one another, that all must be wise, or all foolish.

That he may reign with Christ, to whom the Father has committed all that is His. And as the son of a good father set over all that is his, He shall communicate of His dignity and glory to His faithful and wise stewards, that they also may be above the whole creation.

From this place we learn that there will be a difference of torment in hell, seeing one is here said to be singly a child of hell, another twofold. And we ought to consider here whether it is possible that a man should be generally a child of hell, as a Jew, suppose, or a Gentile, or whether specially so in consequence of some particular sins; that as a righteous man is increased in glory by the abundance of his righteousnesses, so a sinner's punishment is increased manifold by the number of his sins.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who go about the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and when he has been made, you make him a son of gehenna twice as much as you yourselves are.

These things are fittingly said, after the coming of Christ, to the scribes and Pharisees of Jewish words, who diligently go about very many places of the world in order to persuade newcomers to Judaize. For whoever Judaize after the Savior are taught to imitate the disposition of those who said at that time: "Crucify, crucify him", and again "Away with such a one from the earth"; and they are taught also to accuse him, just as then the priests of the people used to accuse him. And it is possible to see them even now, when a robber is being judged and a Christian bears witness to the truth, wishing rather that the imitator of Barabbas be acquitted than the disciple of Christ. All of…

It seems to me that each utterance of divine Scripture is like some kind of seed, whose nature is this: that when it has been cast into the earth, it is regenerated into an ear of grain or into whatever other form of its own kind, and is spread abroad manifold — and the more abundantly, the more either a skilled farmer expends greater labor upon the seeds, or grants the benefit of more fertile soil. So then it comes about that by diligent cultivation a tiny "seed", for example "of mustard, which is the least of all, becomes greater than all herbs and turns into a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and dwell in its branches". So too this utterance, which has now been read to us from the divine volumes, if it finds a skilled and diligent husbandman — though at first touch it may seem meager and brief — once it begins to be cultivated and to be handled with spiritual art, grows into a…

Otherwise; Notwithstanding they were foolish, they yet understood that they must have light to go and meet the bridegroom, that all the lights of their senses might be burning. This also they discerned, that because they had little of the spiritual oil, their lamps would burn dim as darkness drew on. But the wise send the foolish to those that sell, seeing that they had not stored up so much oil, that is, word of doctrine, as would suffice both for themselves to live by, and to teach others, Go ye rather to them that sell, i. e. to the doctors, and buy, i. e. take of them; the price is perseverance, the love of learning, industry, and toil of all who are willing to learn.

And the robbers who were crucified with him reproached him with the same thing.

And in commenting on John we have explained, as best we could, concerning the two robbers who were crucified with Christ, who according to Matthew indeed and Mark both reproached him on the cross, but according to Luke, who says that "one of the hanging robbers blasphemed him, saying: You are the Christ; save yourself and us. But the other, answering, rebuked him, saying: Do you not fear God, seeing that you are in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we receive things worthy of our deeds; but this man has done nothing evil. And he said to Jesus: Remember me when you come into your kingdom. But Jesus, answering, said to him who had rebuked the one blaspheming: "Amen I say to you: today you shall be with me in paradise".

It is fitting, therefore, that at first indeed both robbers should be…

In the Gospel too a woman, taking an alabaster jar of ointment of costly spikenard, poured it over the head and feet of Jesus. Observe diligently what the two women poured over the head of the Savior. For the sinful woman is shown to have poured over his feet, and she who is not called a sinner over his head. Observe, I say, and you will find, in the Gospel reading, that not fables and tales were written by the Evangelists, but mysteries. And so the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment — if what the sinful woman had is to be referred to the feet, and what the woman who was no sinner had, to the head. Nor is it any wonder that the house was filled with the fragrance, since this world has been filled with it. In the same place it is written of Simon the leper and his house. I think that the leper, the prince of this world, is also called "Simon the leper," whose house at…

quotes.quote:
Then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is Christ. Behold, there. Do not believe. For false Christs and false prophets shall arise. And they shall give great signs and wonders, so that even the elect, if it be possible, may be led into error. Behold, I have foretold it to you. But if they say to you: Behold, he is in the wilderness, do not go out; behold, he is in the houses, do not believe. For as lightning goes forth from the east and appears even to the west, so shall be the coming of the Son of man; for wherever the corpse shall be, there shall the eagles be gathered together..

Since we have said that the "abomination of desolation standing in the holy place" is the word of falsehood which appears to stand in the holy place of the scriptures, someone will say: and how, as though it were not standing there, will someone thus say to the disciples of Christ behold, here is Christ.…

Amen I say to you, that this generation shall not pass away, until all these things be done. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

Let us see what this generation is, of which Christ speaks.

And the simple, indeed, refer these words to the destruction of Jerusalem; and they suppose it was said of that generation which existed in the time of Christ and looked upon his suffering, a generation that would not pass away before the destruction of that city came to pass.

But I do not know whether they can expound word for word what he says: "do you not see all these things? amen I say to you, there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be destroyed" down to that which he says: it is near, at the door. For perhaps in some points they will be able, but in others they will not be able at all, and, sufficiently hemmed in, I do not know…

It is also in your power to cast off the image of the serpent as well. Indeed, Scripture calls the evil man a serpent and a brood of vipers. But if you seek confirmation that we are able to change and to cease being serpents, swine, or dogs, let us turn to the words of the Apostle, that the transformation depends on us. … If you were a raging beast and heard the Word, which will tame and domesticate you and which at Its own discretion will turn you into a man — you will never again hear said of you: serpent, brood of vipers. Because, if it were impossible to be rid of these serpents, the serpents residing in the soul on account of its wickedness, then the Savior (or John) would not have said: "Bring forth then fruits worthy of repentance!" Having turned, you will no longer be serpents, broods of vipers.

They that stand where Jesus stands, are they that have the foundations of their souls rested upon Jesus; of whom such as stood firmest are said not to taste death till they see the Word of God; which comes in His kingdom when they see that excellence of God which they cannot see while they are involved in divers sins, which is to taste death, forasmuch as the soul that sinneth, dies. For as life, and the living bread, is He that came down from heaven, so His enemy death is the bread of death. And of these breads there are some that eat but a little, just tasting them, while some eat more abundantly. They that sin neither often, nor greatly, these only taste death; they that have partaken more perfectly of spiritual virtue do not taste it only, but feed ever on the living bread. That He says, Until they see, does not fix any time at which shall be done what had not been done before, but…
Wherefore He does not rebuke them, but goes again and prays, teaching us that we should not faint but should persevere in prayer, until we obtain what we have begun to ask.
Or; Those that believed rebuked them that they should not dishonour Him by styling Him merely Son of David, but should rather say, Son of God, have mercy on us.

Whence also, when He ascended into heaven, He gave command to His disciples that they should loose sinners, for which also He gave them the Holy Spirit. But being loosed, and making progress, and being nourished by the Divinity of the Word, they are held worthy to be sent back to the place whence they were taken, but no more to their former labours, but to preach to them the Son of God, and this is what He signifies when He says, And straightway He will send them.

But when the Son of Man shall come in his glory, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory; and before him shall be gathered all the nations, and the rest. Taken without examination, the passage seems plain, as though it were exhorting people to give and to be generous and turning them away from all inhumanity and stinginess. Let us see, nevertheless, what one ought to look for in it, for the sake of those who suppose there is nothing else in it but an exhortation to kindness. Certainly the whole Church believes that there will be a second and glorious coming of Christ, when the Son of God also, "who was taken up in glory," will thus return here with glory in his own form and his own beauty, so that his body will be such as it was when he had been transfigured on the mountain before the three disciples who had climbed up with him — so that now he may…

Or, The priests may with good reason be called the eyes of the Church, since they are considered her watchmen, but the deacons and the rest her hands, for by them spiritual deeds are wrought; the people are the feet of the body, the Church; and all these it behoves not to spare, if they become an offence to the Church. Or, by the offending hand is understood an act of the mind; a motion of the mind is the offending foot, and a vision of the mind is the sinning eye, which we ought to cut off if they give offence, for thus the acts of the limbs are often put in Scripture for the limbs themselves.

Seeing Peter had confessed Him to be Christ the Son of the living God, because He would not have them preach this in the mean time, He adds, Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ.

Or they then spake of Him in lowly words, as only a great and wonderful man, but as yet proclaimed Him not as the Christ. Yet if any will have it that He was even at the first proclaimed to be Christ, he may say that now He chose that first short announcement of His name to be left in silence and not repeated, that that little which they had heard concerning Christ might be digested into their minds. Or the difficulty may be solved thus: that the former relation concerning their preaching Christ does not belong to the time before His Resurrection, but to the time that should be after the Resurrection; and that the command now given is meant for the time…

Now, having discoursed sufficiently to the multitudes in parables, he sends them away and goes to his own house, where his disciples come to him. His disciples did not go with those he sent away. As many as are more genuine hearers of Jesus first follow him, then having inquired about his house, are permitted to see it. Having come, they saw and stayed with him for all that day, and perhaps some of them even longer. In my opinion, such things are implied in the Gospel according to John.… And if then, unlike the multitudes whom he sends away, we wish to hear Jesus and go to the house and receive something better than the multitudes did, let us become friends of Jesus, so that as his disciples come, we may also come to him when he goes into the house. And having come, let us inquire about the explanation of the parable, whether of the tares of the field, or of any other.

As He had said to the righteous, Come ye, so He says to the wicked, Depart ye, for they who keep God's commandment are near to the Word, and are called that they may be made more near; but they are far from it, though they may seem to stand hard by, who do not His commands; therefore it is said to them, Depart ye, that those who seemed to be living before Him, might be no more seen. It should be remarked, that though He had said to the Saints, Ye blessed of my Father, He says not now, Ye cursed of my Father, because of all blessing the Father is the author, but each man is the origin of his own curse when he does the things that deserve the curse. They who depart from Jesus fall into eternal fire, which is of a very different kind from that fire which we use. For no fire which we have is eternal, nor even of any long continuance. And note, that He does not say, 'the kingdom prepared for…

"And when the days were completed, he hungered. And the devil said to him: If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread". "Tell", he says, "this stone". Which stone? Surely the one the devil was pointing out, the one he wants to be made bread. What sort of temptation is this, that when a son asks his father for bread and the father does not give him a stone, this adversary, crafty and deceitful, should give a stone in place of bread? Is this the whole of what the devil wanted — that a stone should become bread, and that men should feed not on bread but on a stone, which the devil had pointed out in place of bread? I think that even to this day the devil shows a stone and urges each person to say: "tell this stone to become bread". By every temptation with which men were to be tempted, the Lord was tempted first, according to his assumption of the flesh. And he is tempted…

quotes.quote: But since children cannot follow all things that are commanded them, Jesus laid His hands upon them, and leaving virtue in them by His touch, went away from them, seeing they were not able to follow Him, like the other more perfect disciples.
That is, the stone is the gift of God to the whole building, and is wonderful in our eyes, who can discern it with the eyes of the mind.

The graves are the bodies of sinful souls, that is, souls dead to God; but when by God's grace these souls have been raised, their bodies which before were graves, become bodies of Saints, and appear to go out of themselves, and follow Him who rose again, and walk with Him in newness of life; and such as are worthy to have their conversation in heaven enter into the Holy City at divers times, and appear unto many who see their good works.
It is from humility that they declare themselves unworthy of any praise for their good deeds, not that they are forgetful of what they have done. But He shows them His close sympathy with His own.

These things are what "defiles the person" when they come out from the heart and, after they have gone out from it, go through the mouth. Thus if they did not occur outside of the heart but were held by the person somewhere around the heart, not being allowed to be spoken through the mouth, they would very quickly disappear and the person would not be defiled any longer. Therefore the source and beginning of every sin is "evil reasonings." For if these reasonings did not prevail, there would be neither murders nor acts of adultery nor any other of such things. Because of this each one ought to keep one's own heart with all watchfulness.

And one is a scribe "as a disciple to the kingdom of heaven" in the simpler sense, when one comes from Judaism and receives the teaching of Jesus Christ as defined by the church. But one is a scribe in a deeper sense when having received elementary knowledge through the letter of the Scriptures one ascends to things spiritual, which are called the kingdom of heaven. And as each thought is attained, grasped abstractly and proved by example and absolute demonstration, thereby one can understand the kingdom of heaven. Thus one who abounds in knowledge free from error is in the kingdom of the multitude of what are here represented as "heavens." … Hence, so far as Jesus Christ, "who was in the beginning with God, God the Word," has not his home in a soul, the kingdom of heaven is not in it. But when anyone comes close to admission of the Word, to that one the kingdom of heaven is near. But…

Or we may suppose this fulfilled in the case of those Jews who, knowing Christ, believed in Him. But what follows, But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir, come let us kill him, and let us seize on the inheritance, was fulfilled in those who saw Christ, and knew Him to be the Son of God, yet crucified Him.

For as the lightning goes forth from the east and appears as far as the west, so shall the coming of the Son of man be. But we ought to know this also, that the lightning of truth does not appear in some one place of the Scriptures, while from another place of the Scriptures it is not upheld; rather it is upheld from every place of the Scriptures, that is, whether from the Law or from the prophets or from the Gospels or from the writing of the apostles. And this lightning of truth, going forth from the east — that is, from the beginnings of Christ — appears as far as the dispensation of his passion, in which is its setting. And to such a lightning as this is like the coming of the Son of man, that is, of the word of truth. And in this way too we can understand what he says: it goes forth from the east and appears as far as the west. That Christ is the Word and the truth and the wisdom…
The kingdom of heaven is Jesus the Christ himself, who exhorts all people to repentance and draws them to himself by love.

The governor marvelled at His endurance, as knowing that he had power to condemn Him, He yet continued in a peaceful, placid, and immovable prudence and gravity. He marvelled greatly, for it seemed to him a great miracle that Christ, produced before a criminal tribunal, stood thus fearless of death, which all men think so terrible.

Moreover, according to the simple sense of this saying where he says: do all things whatsoever they tell you to do, but do not do according to their works, we say that by these words he wishes to show that there are certain persons in the Church who, as far as speech is concerned, are indeed capable of teaching marvelous things and expound them according to reason, but are unwilling to act according to what they say: whose teaching indeed is to be heard, but whose manner of life is not to be imitated. He therefore rebukes teachers of this kind, who not only do not do the things they teach, but also cruelly and without mercy, and not according to the estimation of the strength of each hearer, but greater than their power, impose burdens: for instance, those who forbid to marry and, away from what is expedient, compel people toward an immoderate purity, who also teach abstinence from…

False witnesses have place when there is any good colour for their testimony. But no pretext was found which could further their falsehoods against Jesus; notwithstanding there were many desirous to do a favour to the Chief Priests. This then is a great testimony in favour of Jesus, that He had lived and taught so irreproachably, that though they were many, and crafty, and wicked, they could find no semblance of fault in Him.

Now the chief priest and the elders and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might deliver him to death, and they found none; and many false witnesses came forward, and they found none (26, 59. 60ᵃ).

And through these things it is made manifest that Jesus "did no sin, nor was there guile in his mouth". But that his life was most pure and altogether beyond reproach, taking away the occasions of those who seek occasions, is demonstrated from this: that his adversaries found not what they might say against him or give a semblance of truth (yet all the priests and the whole council sought it, and could find nothing plausible); for false testimonies then have their place when they are brought forward with some semblance of truth, but against Jesus not even a semblance was found that could lend aid to lies against Jesus — and this, though there were many willing…

By the kingdom of God, He means the mysteries of the kingdom of God, that is, the divine Scriptures, which the Lord committed, first to that former people who had the oracles of God, but secondly to the Gentiles who brought forth fruit. For the word of God is given to none but to him who brings fruit thereof, and the kingdom of God is given to none in whom sin reigns. Whence came it then that it was given to them from whom it was afterwards taken away? Remember that whatever is given is given of free gift. To whom then He let out the vineyard, He let it out not as to elect already and believing; but to whom He gave it, He gave it with a sentence of election.

Take away from him therefore the talent, and give it to the one who has ten talents. You see that the talent is taken away from the wicked and lazy servant, and given to the one who has ten talents. But how something is taken away from someone which had been given to him, and given to another who acts well, so that he may have these things also on top of those which he had acquired — this is not very easy to explain. Yet it is possible, since he who makes a faculty in someone apt in the doctrines of truth can, by his own divinity, God taking away the sufficiency from the one who has used it too lazily, give it to the one who has multiplied it.

For to everyone who has it shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from him who has not, even that which he has shall be taken away from him. For example, to one who has faith, even that which is from ourselves, shall be given the grace…

And after they had crucified him, they divided his garments among themselves, casting lots, and sitting down they kept watch over him (27, 35. 36).

And there are even now those who indeed do not possess him, but possess his garments — the words set down in the Scriptures — and not even these in full but only in part, though the prophet foretold this very mystery which has now been fulfilled. But whether any of his garments was torn apart in that division, or whether each of them remained whole as it had been, and what kind those garments were, we do not read in the three evangelists; but in John we learn that "the soldiers, after they had crucified Christ, took his garments and made four parts, to each soldier a part, but the tunic, since it was not sewn together but woven from the top throughout the whole, they said to one another: let us not tear it apart, but let us cast lots for…

Let us look well whether this precept extends to all sin; for what if any one sin any of those sins which are unto death, such as unnatural crimes, adultery, homicide, or effeminacy, it cannot be meant that such as these are to be admonished privately, and if he hear you, forthwith to say that you have gained him. And not rather first put him out of the Church, or only when remaining obstinate after monition before witnesses, and by the Church? One man, looking at the infinite mercy of Christ, will say, that since the words of Christ make no distinction of sins, it is to go against Christ's mercy to limit His words only to little sins. Another, on the other hand, considering the words carefully, will aver, that they are not spoken of every sin; for that he that is guilty of those great sins is not a brother, but is called a brother, with whom, according to the Apostle, we ought not so…

Do you wish to know that these things agree also with the Gospel precepts? The Lord himself says: "if you see your brother sin, reprove him between yourself and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not hear you, take with you two others or three. But if he does not hear even them, tell the church. But if he does not hear even the church, let him be to you as a heathen and a publican". But the Gospel precept was given more perfectly in this, that it established the manner and discipline of disclosing the sin. For it does not wish you, if perchance you have seen your brother's sin, at once to fly out into public and everywhere to proclaim and divulge another's sins — which would surely be the mark not of one correcting, but rather of one defaming. "Alone", it says, "between yourself and him, rebuke him". For when he who sins sees the mystery kept for…

He, therefore, who is said to baptize "in the Holy Spirit and in fire", has "a winnowing fork in his hand and he will cleanse his threshing floor; and he will gather his wheat into the granary, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire". I wish to find the reason why our Lord has a "winnowing fork", and by what wind blowing the light chaff is snatched hither and thither, while the heavy wheat is carried down into one place; for neither can the wheat and the chaff be separated without wind. I consider that temptations are to be understood in place of the wind, which out of the mingled heap of believers show some to be chaff, others to be wheat. For when your soul has been overcome by some temptation, the temptation does not turn you into chaff, but, since you were chaff — namely light and unbelieving — the temptation reveals you to be what you were hiding. On the contrary,…
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 26

quotes.quote: One thing they know which is true concerning Him; they esteemed Him a Prophet, though not understanding His greatness in respect of His being the Son of God. But the rulers feared the multitude who thought thus of Him, and were ready to fight for Him; for they could not attain to the understanding which the multitude had, seeing they thought nothing worthy concerning Him. Further, know that there are two different kinds of desires to lay hands on Jesus. The desire of the rulers and Pharisees was one kind; another that of the Bride, I held him, and would not let him go; (Song of Sol. 3:4. ch. 7:8.) intending to try Him still further, as she saith, I will get me up into the palm tree, I will lay hold of its height. All who think not rightly concerning His divinity, seek to lay hands on Jesus in order to put Him to death. Other words indeed excepting the word of Christ it is possible to…

Now, keeping in mind what we said above in regard to the passage from Isaiah about the bill of divorce, we will say that the mother of the people separated herself from Christ, her husband, without having received the bill of divorce.Afterward, however, when an unseemly thing was found in her, she did not find favor in his sight, and the bill of divorce was written out for her. When the new covenant called those of the Gentiles to the house of him who had cast away his former wife, it virtually gave the bill of divorce to her who formerly separated from her husband—the law and the Word. Therefore, he also having separated from her, married, so to speak, another, having given into the hands of the former wife the bill of divorce. So they can no longer do what was ordered to them under the law because of the certificate of divorce. And a sign that she has received the bill of divorce is…

Even now do many fight against Jesus with spiritual weapons, to wit, with divers and shifting dogmas concerning God. It deserves enquiry why, when He was known by face to all who dwelt in Judæa, he should have given them a sign, as though they were unacquainted with His person. But a tradition to this effect has come down to us, that not only had He two different forms, one under which He appeared to men, the other into which He was transfigured before His disciples in the mount, but also that He appeared to each man in such degree as the beholder was worthy; in like manner as we read of the manna, that it had a flavour adapted to every variety of use, and as the word of God shows not alike to all. They required therefore a sign by reason of this His transfiguration.

And as they passed by they blasphemed him, wagging their heads and saying: aha, you who were destroying the temple and rebuilding it in three days; free yourself, if you are the Son of God, come down from the cross. Likewise also the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes and the elders and the Pharisees, said: he saved others, himself he cannot save; if he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross and we believe him. He trusts in God; he will free him now if he wills him; for he said, that I am the Son of God.

No one who stands blasphemes Jesus, nor anyone who walks aright; for it was those passing by who blasphemed him (or, as the Greek has it, those going past), who also, once the fence of the vineyard has been broken down by God, gather as their vintage those who have remained; for it is written: "Why have you cast down its fence, and all who pass by the way…
The Lord is able by the might of His divinity to take away his ability from the man who is slack to use it, and to give it to him who has improved his own.

Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him: Where do you wish that we prepare for you to eat the Passover? And Jesus said: Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him, and so forth.

But in Mark he speaks thus: "And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover was being sacrificed, his disciples say to him: Where do you wish that we go and prepare for you to eat the Passover? And he sent two of his disciples, saying: Go into the city, and as you enter a man will meet you carrying a jar of water; and wherever he enters, say to the householder: The Master says: Where is my guest-chamber, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples? And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there prepare for us".

As therefore it appears, it was one and the same day of the Passover, when it was fitting to sacrifice the…

But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up the spirit.

As far as Matthew is concerned—who says that Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and gave up the spirit, but does not make clear what that loud voice was which he cried out again—one could say that he cried out again the same voice which he had cried out above when he said: "My God, my God." But because Luke clearly writes what voice he cried out when he gave up the spirit, saying: "Into thy hands I commend my spirit,"

it is to be understood also in this place that the voice which he cried out again as he gave up the spirit was this one: "Into thy hands I commend my spirit."

If, therefore, to give up the spirit, or (as John writes) to hand over the "spirit," were the very same thing as to die, then what is said in this place, he gave up the spirit, would have to be understood in a plain sense. But now, since the…

(non occ.) She was indeed espoused to Joseph, but not united in wedlock; that is to say, His mother immaculate, His mother incorrupt, His mother pure. His mother! Whose mother? The mother of God, of the Only-begotten, of the Lord, of the King, of the Maker of all things, and the Redeemer of all.

Why does the Evangelist make mention here of "birth," whereas at the start of the Gospel he had said "generation"? For in this place he says, "Now the birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way," but there "The book of the generation." … What then is the difference between "birth" and "generation"? How are either of them to be understood as applied to Christ? Note that this, my spoken word, in its own proper nature, is intangible and invisible. But when it is written down in a book, in a manner of speaking, it takes on a body. It is then both seen and touched. So it is with the fleshless, bodiless Word of God. The Word is neither seen nor described according to his Godhood but becomes, through his incarnation, subject to both sight and description. For this reason there is the "book" of his "generation" as of one who is made flesh. But here the point under investigation is not why he…

Again, turning it over in my mind, I ask why God, when once he had determined that the Savior should be born of a "virgin", did not choose a girl without a betrothed, but rather her especially who had already been "betrothed". And unless I am mistaken, this is the reason: He ought to be born of that virgin who not only had a betrothed, but, as Matthew writes, had already been handed over to a man, although the man did not yet know her, lest her very condition should display the shame of a virgin, if she were seen to be a virgin with a swelling womb. But the one who betrayed him gave them a sign, saying: whomever I shall kiss, that is he, hold him fast. And immediately approaching Jesus he said: hail Rabbi, and he kissed him. But Jesus said to him: friend, to what have you come?

It is worth inquiring for what cause, when Jesus had taught openly through every city and village and synagogue, preaching the word of the Gospel (so that his fame went out into the whole region), and had been made manifest in his face to all who dwelt in Judaea, Judas gave to those sent by the chief priests a sign, as though they did not recognize his likeness, saying: whomever I shall kiss, that is he. But that even those who had come with Judas to seize him had frequently seen him is made manifest from this, that Jesus himself says to the crowds: you have come out to seize me as though against a robber, with swords and clubs: daily I was sitting with you…

But some standing there and hearing him said: This man is calling Elijah … but the others said: Let us see whether Elijah comes and delivers him.

As though they had heard that he called upon God, and had marveled at his prayer on the cross, greater than was the prayer of Jonah praying in the belly of the whale, and had been profited by it, so that even when set amid the most extreme calamities they might not cease to pray to God. And I say that the prayer of Christ was greater than that of Jonah in the belly of the whale on account of the magnitude of the things that are shown forth from it, and on account of the great effect of his voluntary passion.

And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? He says, Friend, upbraiding his hypocrisy; for in Scripture we never find this term of address used to any of the good, but as above, Friend, how camest thou in hither? (Matt. 22:12.) and, Friend, I do thee no wrong. (Matt. 20:13.)

"They are blind guides of blind people." Who are these blind guides? The Pharisees, whose minds "the god of this age has blinded" because they are "unbelieving," since they did not believe in Jesus Christ. The god of this age has blinded them "so that the light of the gospel of the glory of God in the face of Christ would not shine on them." We ought to avoid being guided by those blind persons. Not only should we do this, but we certainly should also listen with caution in the case of those who claim to lead in the way of healthy teaching and ought to apply healthy judgment to what they say. We should do these things so that we ourselves do not appear to be blind because we do not see the meaning of the Scriptures. We would become blind like this if we were guided by the ignorance of people who are blind and people who do not perceive the issues of healthy teaching. If we were led by…

Yet it is not all barely, but all these; for there were other sayings which He must speak before He should be delivered up.

He said not, After two days will be, or will come, the feast of the Passover, but not meaning the ordinary annual Passover, but that Passover such as had never before been, the Passover will be offered.

And it came to pass, after Jesus had finished all these words, that he said to his disciples.

Wishing to show that God has appointed all things in weight and number and measure, he says in a certain place to his mother: "my hour has not yet come", and again: "now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause I came unto this hour", and again: "Father, the hour is come; glorify your Son, that your Son also may glorify you" — so too he appointed the hour of the passion of his Son. Therefore, even though he frequently suffered plots from the Jews, he could suffer nothing while the devil departed from him "until a time", and he could suffer nothing until he had completed all his words which he had purposed to speak to his disciples. For this reason after he had completed all these words, then he said to his disciples. And observe that he did…

The disciples of Christ are better than the common herd; and you may find in the Church such as with more ardent affection come to the word of God; these are Christ's disciples, the rest are only His people. And sometimes He speaks to His disciples alone, sometimes to the multitudes and His disciples together, as here.

The fact that there are such men confessing themselves to be Christians, and admitting the crucified Jesus to be both Lord and Christ, yet not teaching His doctrines, but those of the spirits of error, causes us who are disciples of the true and pure doctrine of Jesus Christ, to be more faithful and stedfast in the hope announced by Him. For what things He predicted would take place in His name, these we do see being actually accomplished in our sight. For he said, "Many shall come in My name, clothed outwardly in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves." And, "There shall be schisms and heresies." And, "Beware of false prophets, who shall come to you clothed outwardly in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves." And, "Many false Christs and false apostles shall arise, and shall deceive many of the faithful." There are, therefore, and there were many, my…

And hear again how Isaiah in express words foretold that He should be born of a virgin; for he spoke thus: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bring forth a son, and they shall say for His name, `God with us.'" For things which were incredible and seemed impossible with men, these God predicted by the Spirit of prophecy as about to come to pass, in order that, when they came to pass, there might be no unbelief, but faith, because of their prediction. But lest some, not understanding the prophecy now cited, should charge us with the very things we have been laying to the charge of the poets who say that Jupiter went in to women through lust, let us try to explain the words. This, then, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive," signifies that a virgin should conceive without intercourse. For if she had had intercourse with any one whatever, she was no longer a virgin; but the power of God…

But if so great a power is shown to have followed and to be still following the dispensation of His suffering, how great shall that be which shall follow His glorious advent! For He shall come on the clouds as the Son of man, so Daniel foretold, and His angels shall come with Him. These are the words: [...he quotes Daniel 7:9-28]

Concerning chastity, He uttered such sentiments as these: "Whosoever looketh upon a woman to lust after her, hath committed adultery with her already in his heart before God." And, "If thy right eye offend thee, cut it out; for it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of heaven with one eye, than, having two eyes, to be cast into everlasting fire." And, "Whosoever shall marry her that is divorced from another husband, committeth adultery."
